questions.prompt: What should minimise mean inside the single browser window?
questions.description: The application will not create operating-system windows, so minimising needs a clear in-workspace behaviour.
questions.recommendedAnswer: Collapse the panel to an edge rail, keep its title visible, and restore it with one click.

options.label: Hide and reopen from a panel menu

questions.prompt: Which workspace behaviours must the first demonstration prove?
questions.description: The requested essentials are preselected; internal floating and layout persistence are included because they materially affect the window-system choice.
questions.recommendedAnswer: Prove docking and splitting, tabbing, resizing, closing and reopening, minimising and restoring, maximising and restoring, internal floating, plus saved and resettable layouts.

options.label: Float panels inside the browser tab
Save and reset the workspace layout

questions.prompt: What should the panels contain while we test the workspace?
questions.description: Realistic TradeMaker content lets us assess whether the window system supports the eventual guided news-analysis experience.
questions.recommendedAnswer: Use a realistic but clearly simulated TradeMaker story: news source, extracted evidence, primary security, related companies, wider market, and guided interpretation.

questions.prompt: Which initial visual direction should the demonstrator use?
questions.description: This is a workspace default, not a final brand decision. The implementation will use Tailwind and daisyUI.
questions.recommendedAnswer: Use a restrained dark trading-workbench theme by default and include a light-theme switch so both remain usable.

questions.prompt: How much of this demonstrator should become the foundation of the real application?
questions.description: This determines whether we optimise for rapid learning, long-lived structure, or a deliberate mixture of both.
questions.recommendedAnswer: Keep the monorepo, tooling, tested workspace shell, and panel contracts; treat all sample analysis content as replaceable.

options.label: Keep the shell, replace the mock content
